questions.question: Why is −7 smaller than −2 even though 7 is bigger than 2?
questions.expected_answer: On the number line −7 lies further to the left than −2, and further left means smaller; in money terms, owing 7 is worse than owing 2.

questions.question: State the rule that turns any subtraction of integers into an addition, and use it on 4 − (−3).
questions.expected_answer: Subtracting a number is the same as adding its opposite: a − b = a + (−b). So 4 − (−3) = 4 + 3 = 7.

questions.question: A temperature of −4 °C rises by 6 °C. What is the new temperature and which addition rule did you use?
questions.expected_answer: −4 + 6 = 2 °C. Different signs: subtract the smaller absolute value from the larger (6 − 4 = 2) and take the sign of the larger, which is positive.
